messages.subject: unstable results with stepwiseqtl
messages.subject_clean: unstable results with stepwiseqtl
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,

While checking a loop with the stepwiseqtl() function, I realized that the stepwiseqtl() results were unstable for some variables.

Thus, I ran 10 times this single command line for a given variable:

smdoy<-stepwiseqtl(don,pheno.col=5, max.qtl=8, method="hk",  penalties=calc.penalties(p2don[[4]],alpha=0.05), model="normal",incl.markers=TRUE, refine.locations=TRUE,additive.only=FALSE, scan.pairs=FALSE, keeplodprofile=F, keeptrace=T, verbose=F,tol=1e-4, maxit=1000)

7 times out of 10, I got this outcome:

      name chr    pos n.gen
Q1  1...@43.0   1 43.000     4
Q2   3...@9.0   3  9.000     4
Q3  4...@15.6   4 15.649     4
Q4  8...@59.8   8 59.781     4
Q5  1...@1.0  13  1.000     4
Q6 1...@16.4  14 16.356     4
Q7 1...@13.0  17 13.000     4

  Formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4 + Q5 + Q6 + Q7 + Q3:Q6 + Q2:Q4

  pLOD:  0.956

but 3 times out of 10, I got this different outcome :
      name chr pos n.gen
Q1 1...@13.0  17  13     4

  Formula: y ~ Q1

  pLOD:  0.366

Genotypic probabilities were calcultated this way:

don<-calc.genoprob(don, step=1, map.function=c("kosambi"), error.prob=0.0005)

What may be the reason for this ?
And how would you advise to proceed ? Systematically run stepwiseqtl several times and retain the most frequent outcome ?

I apologize if I have missed any comments already published on this topic.

Thank you in advance for your help.

Agnes

messages.subject: confusing scanone output
messages.subject_clean: confusing scanone output
messages.body_plain:
I am using scanone to map qtls on a data set derived from ngs. I have  35K variants as markers and am wish to identify QTLs for a single trait using 96 segregants of a haploid micro-organism in a simple cross between two strains. The genotypes have been assigned as AA or AB as for a BC. Prior to running scanone I just ran calc.genoprob as advised in the short tour tutorial.  Now the problem is that I have many loci that are giving LOD scores in excess of 3 with no obvious peaks. In the first round I noticed that I had one extreme outlier in the data set but the problem persisted even after removing that. I assume that the source of the problem is the large number of markers and that the high LOD scores are arising by chance.  How does one deal with this sort of problem and get a scan plot out that is informative as to whether there are any QTL detectable.

Thank you.

William

messages.body_plain:
I've not seen this before. There is randomness in refineqtl(), in the order in which QTL are considered, and this may lead to the algorithm getting caught in a local optimum in some instances.

In general, I'd try not to rely on the model that stepwiseqtl() provides, but use it as a starting point for exploring the set of models with similar penalized LOD scores.

You might also look at the trace of models that stepwiseqtl() visited. What was different between the times it selected a 7-QTL model and the times it selected the 1-QTL model?

karl

messages.body_plain:
scanone performs calculations at the markers plus at positions between markers ("pseudomarkers") at a density defined by the step argument in calc.genoprob (or, for method="imp", sim.geno).

You could rerun calc.genoprob with step=0, and then rerun scanone, and the results will not include any such pseudomarkers.

Or you could remove them afterwards by subsetting with your marker names, or search for the pattern c[chr].loc[pos]. Here's an example.

   data(hyper)
   hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
   out <- scanone(hyper)

   # use marker names
   out_onlymarkers_1 <- out[markernames(hyper),]

   # search for pseudomarkers to remove
   out_onlymarkers_2 <- out[!grepl("^c.+\\.loc-*[0-9]+", rownames(out)), ]

karl

> I'm running a multi-QTL analysis using makeqtl and fitqtl, and am wondering if there's a way to do a permutation test (as in the single-QTL analysis with scanone) for the multi-QTL model?

I recommend using the stepwiseqtl() function and the related penalized LOD score criterion for comparing multiple-QTL models. See Ch 9 of the R/qtl book (http://rqtl.org/book) and Broman and Speed (2002) and Manichaikul et al (2009).
https://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/publications/jrssb.pdf
https://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/publications/multiqtl.pdf

> Additionally, I need to print the position and LOD of all markers in my genetic map. Is there a way to do this for the multi-QTL analysis similar to scanone for the single-QTL analysis?

The result of refineqtl(), when you use keeplodprofile=TRUE, includes the LOD profiles as an attribute.
The lodprofile is a list, with each component corresponding to a different QTL and being a table with chromosome, position, and profile LOD score.

  data(fake.bc)
  fake.bc <- calc.genoprob(fake.bc, step=1)
  out <- scanone(fake.bc)
  summary(out, threshold=3)
  qtl <- makeqtl(fake.bc, chr=c(2,5), pos=c(34, 16), what="prob")
  rqtl <- refineqtl(fake.bc, qtl=qtl, keeplodprofile=TRUE, method="hk")
  lprof <- attr(rqtl, "lodprofile")
  lprof[[1]]
  lprof[[2]]

karl
